Subject: MSA / Order Form — proposed approach to IP/3rd‑party claims

Jonas — thanks for the call earlier. Attached is our internal redline of the MSA + Order Form (Aurora_MSA_Redline_v2.docx) and a short SLA table for evidence/notice timelines. Two items we want to resolve before we proceed:

1) Defense ownership for third‑party IP claims. Aurora is prepared to accept a defend obligation for claims alleging direct infringement by our specific use of the service, provided Redwood retains the right to participate and the parties agree a single lead counsel.

2) Evidence preservation & handback timing — our procurement team needs a firm timeline and point of contact for forensic evidence collection (examples in the attached spreadsheet).

High‑level ask: can Redwood accept a defense obligation for covered IP claims with a dollar cap tied to the order form value OR, alternatively, keep reimburse-only but agree a narrow preserve/assist workflow with guaranteed response SLAs?

Samir will handle procurement logistics on our end; Elena from ARC will shepherd legal redlines. If you can send your preferred language by EOD Monday it would keep us on schedule.

Thanks,
Claire Donovan
VP, Procurement — Aurora Analytics
Aurora Analytics | +1 415 555 0143

Claire — appreciate the clear asks and the attachments. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and Ben (sales ops) to propose concrete language.

Quick context from our side: Redwood’s standard play is defend-for-IP claims that directly implicate our model code or model artifacts; for AI‑output/derivative allegations we usually offer indemnity-by-reimbursement or a carveout, depending on risk. We’re open to a hybrid: defend where the claim is clearly about Redwood’s service implementation, reimburse for customer prompt/output claims, and a shared evidence workflow.

Kimberly — can you weigh in on (a) whether we can accept lead defense for Aurora claims subject to a cap tied to the order, and (b) an operational SLA for evidence/forensic handback we can commit to?

Ben — FYI, this will impact the order form pricing band and whether we trigger a reserved capacity review.

Cheers,
Jonas

Subject: Re: MSA / Order Form — defense ownership & third‑party claim split (Aurora Analytics)

Claire / team — thanks for the redline. Below is Redwood’s proposed compromise language and the implementation notes; I’m attaching a short clause snippet as plain text in the body for quick review. See attached doc for a tracked redline.

Proposed compromise (summary):
- Redwood agrees to assume defense ("Right to Defend") for third‑party claims alleging direct infringement of a third party’s intellectual property by Redwood’s Service, provided that:
  a) Redwood notifies Aurora promptly and Aurora cooperates in the defense;
  b) Redwood has the right to control the defense, but Aurora may retain separate counsel at its own expense;
  c) Redwood may not settle a claim that admits fault or imposes obligations on Aurora without Aurora’s prior written consent (which shall not be unreasonably withheld).
- For claims alleging infringement arising from customer inputs or customer‑provided data (including prompts, fine‑tuning artifacts, or derivative outputs), Redwood will indemnify by reimbursement of reasonable defense costs and damages up to the Order Form cap.
- Cap: Parties agree a limit on indemnity exposure equal to 3x the twelve‑month committed spend in the Order Form for claims other than those for IP infringement caused solely by Redwood. For Redwood‑controlled IP infringement claims (per first bullet), Redwood will accept defense but not exceed an aggregate cap equal to 5x the twelve‑month committed spend.
- Evidence & preservation: Redwood will provide a named technical contact and a 72‑hour acknowledgement SLA for evidence requests, with an initial preservation window of 30 days and a secure handback procedure defined in the Order Form (see SLA spreadsheet).

Clause snippet (for redline):
"Subject to the limitations and caps set forth in the applicable Order Form, Redwood shall defend and indemnify Customer from and against any third party claim that the Redwood Service, as provided by Redwood (excluding Customer Inputs), infringes such third party’s issued patents or copyrights. Customer shall promptly notify Redwood of any such claim and shall reasonably cooperate in the defense. Redwood shall have the right to control the defense and settlement of any such claim; provided that Redwood shall not settle any claim in a manner that admits fault by Customer or imposes obligations on Customer without Customer’s prior written consent (not to be unreasonably withheld). For claims relating to Customer Inputs, Redwood’s indemnification obligation shall be limited to reimbursement of reasonable defense costs and damages up to the cap set forth in the Order Form."

Implementation notes:
- We need Aurora to accept the cap formula; if Aurora needs a flat dollar cap we can convert the multiplier.
- We can operationalize the evidence SLA via a dedicated shared ticket (we recommend a secure SFTP drop for evidence handback and provide a named Redwood engineer).
- If Aurora requires lead counsel approval rights beyond the consent carveout, that’s an exec‑level negotiation (may require legal ops approval).

I’ll prepare a tracked redline by EOD and attach.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
